rules_text:
Rules summary Game of Trains - Simple Rules Summary Goal Be the first player to arrange your train cards in ascending order . Setup Each player starts with their own train line arranged in descending order . Each card has: a number a special power First Round On the first round, players may: draw a card replace one card in their own train line Each Turn After That On your turn, choose one of these options: Draw and replace Draw a card from the draw pile and replace one card in your train line. Use a special power Take one face-up card from the middle of the table and use its special power. What Happens to Cards When you replace a card in your train line, the old card goes face-up into the middle of the table. Cards in the middle can later be taken and used for their special powers. After a special power is used, that card is discarded. Special Powers Special powers can do such things as: swap two cards (has 2 rounded arrows to show if swapping next to each other OR has round arrow card rounded arrow to show swap with a card in-between ie swap 3 2 1 to become 1 2 3). move a card two spaces left or two spaces right. Has two arrows that face left or right. affect all players (cards with the x, affect first card, middle or last which will change for all players without another card locked to it) has x card card, card x card or card card x destroy cards (the x card that removes first, middle or last card previously mentioned). and other actions (lock cards to escape the x actions, although you can move them still) . Has a padlock on it and will sit behind the card you choose to lock. How to Win Keep taking turns until one player has their train line in ascending order . That player wins.

community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Great graphics. Very bad game. Rating after one 4 player game.  I don't know whether the game terminates at some point. The 'remove wagons from all players' cards just mess with the order. There was never any 'lock' card available for a player who could use it (action grabbed by other players, and card discarded after moving the wagon).  In addition, in a 4 player game, it is possible that one player *never* has an action card available, and just has to draw and replace from the stack each turn. Not just theorectically - it happened in our game.   Maybe playable with 3. Don't try it with 4.

[Rating: 2/10] Just horrible game. Sequencing has been done so many times - this game adds nothing to the genre.  Gullotine, which is just so-so, is 100 times more fun than this.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Only played this once, waiting for the chef to prepare our Thai carry-out. Fairly unlikely to play it again except while waiting for a plane. Its main convenience is that the box, for once, exactly contains the game, and is little bigger than an external hard drive. The game consists of using card draws to race to sort an ordinal sequence from small-to-large to large-to-small, most of the moves being simple exchanges of neighbouring cards. Probably gets better as you get better at it.

[Rating: 4/10] A very abstract game - the theme is extremely week. But the graphic artist seems to be a fan of Game of Thrones and old TV series. Very much to discover here. The game itself is ok'ish, I guess.

[Rating: 4/10] Too simple and because of that too luck heavy. Should have checked it out first....

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Rack-o with special powers...and a train theme. Cards were somewhat comical to see what was illustrated. Game was fine but nothing that stood out and I couldn't decide if I enjoyed this more than Rack-o or not (there's an ancient American game....)

[Rating: 4/10] An abstract card game where you are trying to reorganize your trains (cards) from descending order to ascending order. You either draw a card and put it down on your train or you take a power from the discard from previously discarded trains  Some take that but it was light in our game since that move doesn't advance your position.  Definitely boring and not much here. I don't really see anything that interests me

[Rating: 4/10] Weird game. Only played two player - is likely better with a few more - but I'd be more than happy to not play this game again. Not necessarily "bad", we just found it to be a little bland for our tastes.

[Rating: 4/10] Very aggravating game. Just when you think you're making some progress, you get dealt another random card that might hurt or help you immensely. Lucky players will therefore be much more likely to win the game. It's just too random and arbitrarily swingy for me to enjoy much. The special powers don't improve the game: they just make it more random and arbitrarily swingy.

[Rating: 4/10] It's very abstract, it's fairly chaotic, and I'm not sure there's any skill in finishing faster than somebody else but it's also very quick and harmless so I wouldn't actually mind playing it again if anyone insisted.

[Rating: 4/10] Somewhat difficult if you are not getting the wright cards. No chance to recovery.
